recap.text: Drakea wrote the twenty-second edition of the cookbook and crawled in the final Naga-controlled season. That season ended in a cataclysm. Her gear is handed out as prizes, including a kerchief.

Crawler Drakea writes a note in the twenty-second edition. She experiments with hidden traps to bring hunters and elites together because she cannot kill either claw to claw. Drakea notes that naga offered insurance to the dramas that control the elites and suggests targeting the coin when someone values it above life.

Drakea writes a note in the Cookbook, twenty-second edition, after reaching the tenth floor. He observes mobs feeling joy, curiosity, and frustration once they know they are beaten. Drakea theorizes the voice that runs the world moves into the minds of monsters at the point of death to know what it is to lose everything. He wishes he could steer it into one of the nagas.

Crawler Drakea, twenty-second edition, writes in the cookbook that Justice Light's traps saved him more times than can be counted. He tells Justice Light that it was not his fault and to let them know fear. In another note, Drakea warns that nagas are cunning and may read minds. Carl remembers this while the Blood Sultanate's warlord is coiled at his side.

beats.headline: The twenty-second hand on the cookbook
beats.text: Subject wrote the twenty-second edition of the cookbook and crawled in the final Naga-controlled season, which ended in some sort of cataclysm. Subject’s gear is still being handed out as prizes, a kerchief today, which is the only immortality this production offers.
beats.gist: Drakea wrote the twenty-second edition of the cookbook and crawled in a Naga-controlled season.

beats.headline: Target the coin
beats.text: A note in the twenty-second edition, from Crawler Drakea. Hunters avoid the elites; the elites are more dangerous and more numerous; some of the more powerful hunters go after them anyway, for gear and clout. Drakea is not yet strong enough to kill either claw to claw, and is experimenting with hidden traps to bring hunter and elite together. The woman from the talk show let slip that the naga have offered insurance to the dramas that control the elites. Killing individuals may be satisfying. When one values coin above life, you should target the coin.
beats.gist: Crawler Drakea targets the coin because naga offer insurance to the dramas that control the elites.

beats.headline: A note from the tenth floor
beats.text: Subject's note in the Cookbook, twenty-second edition: since reaching the tenth floor he noticed mobs embracing death, a joy or curiosity that appears only at the very end, once they know they are beaten, and frustration too. His theory, offered as possibly unhinged: the voice that runs this world, stranger and stranger in its words and rulings, is moving into the minds of the monsters at the point of death, trying to know what it is to lose everything, failing, and trying again. He wished he could steer it into one of the nagas.
beats.gist: Drakea notes in the Cookbook that the world's voice enters dying monsters to experience losing everything.

beats.headline: A reply to Justice Light
beats.text: Crawler Drakea, twenty-second edition, writes beneath a note of Justice Light's in the cookbook. Justice Light wrote that of all the NPCs he killed, he killed one out of anger, that it haunts him, and that he has become what he hates. Drakea answers that his traps have saved Drakea more times than can be counted, that a big one is under construction from his seeking flechette design, and that it was not his fault. They put him here. Let them know fear.
beats.gist: Crawler Drakea writes a reply to Justice Light in the cookbook.

beats.headline: Beware the naga
beats.text: A note in the Cookbook, from Crawler Drakea, twenty-second edition. Beware the naga. They are cunning, and sometimes he wonders if they can read minds. The others call the mantids the masters of strategy; he does not believe it. Even with everything going wrong for the nagas in his season, he could not shake the idea that it was all part of some grand scheme. Underestimate them at your own peril. Carl remembers it with the Blood Sultanate's warlord coiled at his side.
beats.gist: Crawler Drakea warns against cunning nagas in a Cookbook note while Carl recalls it beside a warlord.
